answer_text:
Work in the polynomial ring over the field \(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\), which we denote \(\mathbb{F}_2[x]\).

We want an ideal \(I\) such that

\[
\mathbb{F}_2[x]/I
\]

is a field with \(8=2^3\) elements. Since \(\mathbb{F}_2[x]/I\) will be a field iff \(I\) is maximal, and maximal ideals in \(\mathbb{F}_2[x]\) are generated by monic irreducible polynomials, we should choose an irreducible polynomial of degree \(3\).

Consider

\[
f(x)=x^3+x+1 \in \mathbb{F}_2[x].
\]

It has no roots in \(\mathbb{F}_2\):

\[
f(0)=1,\qquad f(1)=1+1+1=1 \pmod 2.
\]

Since \(f\) is a cubic polynomial, having no root in \(\mathbb{F}_2\) implies that it is irreducible. Therefore the ideal

\[
I=(x^3+x+1)
\]

is maximal, so the quotient

\[
\mathbb{F}_2[x]/(x^3+x+1)
\]

is a field. As an \(\mathbb{F}_2\)-vector space, it has basis

\[
\{1,x,x^2\},
\]

so it has \(2^3=8\) elements.

Thus one suitable ideal is

\[
\boxed{I=(x^3+x+1)}.
\]
